effect: All three pathways are fitted, and the result explains how touch and muscle stretch provide different sensory information.

reason: The completed arm pathways need to connect to the brain and spinal cord to meet the goal.

effect: The completed arm connects sensory signals to the brain and spinal cord and motor commands back to muscle, clarifying how feedback can help adjust movement.
reaction: The two-way connection brings the separate pathways together in a satisfying way.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the completed arm to the brain and spinal cord was most worthwhile because the result explains how incoming sensory information can help coordinate outgoing commands.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the motor and stretch pathways was predictable once the slots appeared, and those results added little explanation on their own.

surprise.text: I expected the skin and touch fibres to combine directly; instead, compatibility feedback attached the skin to the arm and revealed the pathway slots.

arbitrary.text: The need to attach skin before the motor pathway was not clear from the initial descriptions. The failed attempt did not explain that dependency, though the later feedback revealed it.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the final connection made me curious about how the responsive arm depends on the rest of the body, though I would hope for more explanation during the intermediate fittings.
